name: component-file-missing
summary: A component whose file does not exist yet.
explanation: The design may name a file before it is written, so this is work to do, not breakage. Write the file, or fix the path (relative to the repo root).
query:
SELECT record, 'Component ' || record || ' names ' || file || ', which does not exist yet.' AS message
FROM file_facts
WHERE kind = 'component' AND NOT file_exists
ORDER BY record

name: component-outside-layer
summary: Once a domain has layers, each of its components sits in one of them.
explanation: This works as use cases sit in capabilities. A domain with no layers may hold its components itself. Move the component into one of the domain's layers; its ID does not change.
query:
SELECT c.id AS record,
       'Component ' || c.id || ' sits directly under domain ' || c.domain_id || ', which has layers; move it into the layer it belongs to.' AS message
FROM component c
WHERE c.layer_id IS NULL
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM layer l WHERE l.domain_id = c.domain_id)
ORDER BY record

name: component-satisfies-nothing
summary: A component that satisfies no obligation.
explanation: A component exists to design or implement something the product owes, so it links each obligation it serves with a link of a `design` relation such as `satisfies`. One with no such link has no purpose the spec can see: it is a leftover, or its purpose is unwritten. Shared infrastructure is no exception: link the requirements, domain rules or pattern rules it makes possible. Link what the component designs or implements with "satisfies", or remove it.
query:
SELECT c.id AS record,
       'Component ' || c.id || ' satisfies no obligation; link each requirement, domain rule or pattern rule it '
       || 'designs or implements with "satisfies" (for shared infrastructure, the ones it makes possible), or remove it.' AS message
FROM component c
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM link l JOIN meta_relation r ON r.name = l.relation AND r.role = 'design' WHERE l.source_id = c.id)
ORDER BY record

name: design-flow-deepens-nothing
summary: A technical flow that deepens no flow.
explanation: A technical flow says how the system carries out a flow, so it names that flow with `deepens`. One that deepens nothing is design with no flow to carry out: the flow is missing, or the link is. Link the flow it carries out with `deepens`, or write the flow first.
query:
SELECT d.id AS record, 'Technical flow ' || d.id || ' deepens no flow; link the flow it carries out with "deepens".' AS message
FROM design_flow d
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM deepens x WHERE x.source_id = d.id)
ORDER BY record

name: domain-named-for-technology
summary: A domain is named for a technology layer or delivery channel rather than a business capability.
explanation: A domain is a vertical slice of business capability: it owns its records and rules, its views, its code and its tests, and technology is a layer inside its Design stage. A domain whose title or domain code (its ID after the product prefix, such as LEND in TL-LEND) names a technology splits one capability across several domains. The words are web app, frontend, front end, backend, back end, API, UI, server, database, DB, desktop, mobile, engine, infrastructure, infra and Electron, matched as whole words in any letter case, with or without a space or hyphen inside the two-word ones, and in the plural. Only the title and code are read, never the description. Name the domain for the capability it serves, and make the technology a layer in each domain's Design stage.
query:
SELECT id AS record,
       'Domain ' || id || ' is named for a technology, not a business capability: '
       || CASE WHEN in_title <> '' THEN 'its title "' || trim(title) || '" says "' || in_title || '"' ELSE '' END
       || CASE WHEN in_title <> '' AND in_code <> '' THEN ' and ' ELSE '' END
       || CASE WHEN in_code <> '' THEN 'its code ' || code || ' says "' || in_code || '"' ELSE '' END
       || '; name the domain for the capability it serves, and make the technology a layer in each domain''s Design stage.' AS message
FROM (
  SELECT id, title, code,
         regexp_extract(lower(title), '(^|[^a-z])(' || words || ')([^a-z]|$)', 2) AS in_title,
         regexp_extract(lower(code), '(^|[^a-z])(' || words || ')([^a-z]|$)', 2) AS in_code
  FROM (
    SELECT id, title, CASE WHEN starts_with(id, product_id || '-') THEN substr(id, length(product_id) + 2) ELSE id END AS code
    FROM domain
  ),
  (SELECT 'web[ -]?apps?|front[ -]?ends?|back[ -]?ends?|apis?|uis?|servers?|databases?|dbs?|desktops?|mobile'
          || '|engines?|infrastructure|infra|electron' AS words)
)
WHERE in_title <> '' OR in_code <> ''
ORDER BY record

name: domain-rule-involves
summary: A domain rule under its domain names the aggregates it ties together with `involves`; a rule under an aggregate or entity names none.
explanation: A domain rule sits on the aggregate, or the entity, it is about. One that holds across aggregates, such as two records saved together or a lifecycle rule for every record in the domain, sits under the domain alone (no aggregate_id) and says with `involves` which aggregates it ties together. Such a rule is reported when it involves fewer than two aggregates: a rule about one aggregate belongs under that aggregate. It is also reported, once per link, for each aggregate it involves from another domain, since a rule across domains is a domain event's job: one domain raises the event and the other reacts to it. A rule under an aggregate or an entity that uses `involves` is reported too, since its place already says what it is about. Name the aggregates, move a one-aggregate rule under its aggregate, or drop the link.
query:
WITH rules AS (
  SELECT r.id, r.domain_id,
         CASE WHEN r.entity_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'entity' WHEN r.aggregate_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'aggregate' ELSE 'domain' END AS parent_kind,
         coalesce(r.entity_id, r.aggregate_id, r.domain_id) AS parent
  FROM domain_rule r
),
involved AS (
  SELECT i.source_id AS rule, i.target_id AS target, a.domain_id AS target_domain
  FROM involves i JOIN aggregate a ON a.id = i.target_id
)
SELECT r.id AS record,
       'Domain rule ' || r.id || ' sits under the domain ' || r.parent || ' but involves '
       || CASE count(i.target) WHEN 0 THEN 'no aggregate; name with involves the two or more aggregates it ties together, or move it under the aggregate it is about.'
          ELSE 'only ' || min(i.target) || '; a rule about one aggregate belongs under it, so move it under ' || min(i.target)
               || ', or name with involves every aggregate it ties together.' END AS message
FROM rules r LEFT JOIN involved i ON i.rule = r.id
WHERE r.parent_kind = 'domain'
GROUP BY r.id, r.parent
HAVING count(i.target) < 2
UNION ALL
SELECT r.id,
       'Domain rule ' || r.id || ' involves ' || i.target || ', an aggregate of ' || i.target_domain || ', not of its own domain ' || r.parent
       || '; a rule across domains is a domain event''s job, so have one domain raise an event and the other react to it.'
FROM rules r JOIN involved i ON i.rule = r.id
WHERE r.parent_kind = 'domain' AND i.target_domain <> r.domain_id
UNION ALL
SELECT r.id,
       'Domain rule ' || r.id || ' sits under the ' || r.parent_kind || ' ' || r.parent || ' and involves '
       || string_agg(i.target, ', ' ORDER BY i.target)
       || '; its place already says what it is about, so drop involves, or move it under its domain if it holds across aggregates.'
FROM rules r JOIN involved i ON i.rule = r.id
WHERE r.parent_kind IN ('aggregate', 'entity')
GROUP BY r.id, r.parent, r.parent_kind
ORDER BY record, message

name: entity-fields
summary: Each entity lists the fields it keeps, and each domain event the fields it carries.
explanation: An entity's fields are its entity_field rows and a domain event's its event_field rows, each with a name, a meaning and a type, so the domain model says what each record holds. An entity or event with none says nothing about its data. Add its fields.
query:
SELECT e.id AS record, 'Entity ' || e.id || ' lists no fields; add the fields it keeps, each with its meaning and type.' AS message
FROM entity e
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM entity_field f WHERE f.entity_id = e.id)
UNION ALL
SELECT e.id, 'Event ' || e.id || ' lists no fields; add the fields it carries, each with its meaning and type.'
FROM domain_event e
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM event_field f WHERE f.domain_event_id = e.id)
ORDER BY record, message

name: entity-unreferenced
summary: A child entity that its aggregate's root does not reach.
explanation: Each child entity is a part of its aggregate's root, so a `has_one` or `has_many` reaches it from the root, directly or through other children of the same aggregate. Links that cross aggregates (has-crosses-aggregate) and `refers_to` links do not count. Link the child from the root or from another child with `has_one` or `has_many`.
query:
WITH RECURSIVE
  roots AS (SELECT aggregate_id, id AS root FROM entity WHERE role = 'root'),
  parts AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT l.source_id AS source, l.target_id AS target
    FROM (SELECT source_id, target_id FROM has_one UNION ALL SELECT source_id, target_id FROM has_many) l
    JOIN entity s ON s.id = l.source_id
    JOIN entity t ON t.id = l.target_id AND t.aggregate_id = s.aggregate_id
  ),
  reached (id) AS (
    SELECT root FROM roots
    UNION
    SELECT p.target FROM parts p JOIN reached r ON r.id = p.source
  )
SELECT e.id AS record,
       'Child entity ' || e.id || ' is not reached from ' || e.aggregate_id || '''s root ' || r.root
       || ' by has_one or has_many; link it from ' || r.root || ' or from the child it is a part of.' AS message
FROM entity e
JOIN roots r ON r.aggregate_id = e.aggregate_id
WHERE e.role = 'child' AND e.id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM reached)
ORDER BY record

name: event-tense
summary: A domain event's title reads as something that happened, in the past tense.
explanation: An event is named for what happened, such as Loan opened or Payment sent. The check is a heuristic over the title's words, in any letter case and split at anything but a letter: the title passes when its last word, or any word after its first (the word after a one-word subject, as in Loan became overdue), is a past form. A past form is a word of four or more letters ending in "-ed", other than the few such words that are not verbs in the past (need, seed, feed, speed, breed, bleed, embed, proceed, exceed, succeed, hundred, naked, sacred, wicked), or one of the irregular past forms the query lists. The heuristic can miss a past form it does not know, so this is a warning. Name the event in the past tense, as what happened (Tool returned, not Return tool), or add the word to the check's list if it is a past form the check does not know.
query:
SELECT e.id AS record,
       'Event ' || e.id || ' is titled "' || trim(e.title)
       || '", which does not read as past tense; name it for what happened, such as "Loan opened" or "Tool returned".' AS message
FROM domain_event e
WHERE regexp_matches(lower(e.title), '[a-z]')
  AND e.id NOT IN (
    SELECT w.id
    FROM (
      SELECT id, unnest(words) AS word, unnest(generate_series(1, len(words))) AS position, len(words) AS count
      FROM (SELECT id, string_split(trim(regexp_replace(lower(title), '[^a-z]+', ' ', 'g')), ' ') AS words FROM domain_event)
    ) w
    WHERE (w.position > 1 OR w.position = w.count)
      AND (list_contains(string_split(
      'arose arisen ate eaten awoke awoken became begun began bent bound bit bitten blew blown broke broken bred '
      || 'brought built burnt bought caught chose chosen came cost crept cut dealt dug did done drew drawn dreamt '
      || 'drank drunk drove driven fell fallen fed felt fought found fled flew flown forbade forbidden forgot '
      || 'forgotten forgave forgiven froze frozen got gotten gave given went gone grew grown hung had heard hid '
      || 'hidden hit held hurt kept knew known laid led leant learnt left lent let lit lost made meant met mistook '
      || 'mistaken overdone overran overridden overrode overtaken overtook paid put quit read rebuilt redone remade '
      || 'reran rerun reset resent resold retook retaken rewound rewrote rewritten rode ridden rang rung rose risen '
      || 'ran run said saw seen sought sold sent set shook shaken shone shot showed shown shut sang sung sank sunk '
      || 'sat slept slid spoke spoken sped spent spun split spread sprang sprung stood stole stolen stuck struck '
      || 'swore sworn swept swam swum swung took taken taught tore torn told thought threw thrown understood undid '
      || 'undone upheld upset withdrew withdrawn withheld woke woken wore worn won wound wrote written', ' '), w.word)
           OR (length(w.word) >= 4 AND w.word LIKE '%ed' AND NOT list_contains(string_split(
      'need seed feed speed breed bleed embed proceed exceed succeed hundred naked sacred wicked', ' '), w.word)))
  )
ORDER BY record

name: event-unheard
summary: A domain event that nothing reacts to.
explanation: An event is worth naming when something changes because it happened: an aggregate, which may sit in another aggregate or domain, a use case that starts, or a component that handles it, each linking to the event with `reacts_to`. An event kept only for the record can be fine, so this is a warning. Link what changes, starts or runs when the event happens to it with `reacts_to`, or leave the event unheard on purpose.
query:
SELECT e.id AS record,
       'Nothing reacts to event ' || e.id || ' (' || e.title || '). That can be fine for an event kept for the '
       || 'record; otherwise link the aggregate that changes, the use case that starts or the component that handles it '
       || 'to ' || e.id || ' with reacts_to.' AS message
FROM domain_event e
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM reacts_to r WHERE r.target_id = e.id)
ORDER BY record

name: flow-fulfills-differs-from-steps
summary: A flow with steps fulfills something none of its steps fulfills.
explanation: Once a flow has steps, what the flow fulfills is the union of what its steps fulfill, so each `fulfills` link belongs on the step that does it. A flow with steps may leave its own `fulfills` out: its steps' links are enough. Move the link onto the step that carries it out.
query:
SELECT DISTINCT f.id AS record,
       'Flow ' || f.id || ' fulfills ' || l.target_id || ', but none of its steps does; move the link onto the step that carries it out.' AS message
FROM flow f
JOIN fulfills l ON l.source_id = f.id
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM flow_step s WHERE s.flow_id = f.id)
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM flow_step s JOIN fulfills sl ON sl.source_id = s.id WHERE s.flow_id = f.id AND sl.target_id = l.target_id)
ORDER BY record, message

name: flow-step-fulfills-outside-flow
summary: A flow step fulfills something its flow does not carry out.
explanation: A step carries out part of its flow, so what it fulfills belongs to a use case the flow carries out. For a step under flow F, a `fulfills` target is inside F when it is a requirement of a use case F carries out; a domain rule one of those use cases applies; a rule of a pattern one of them, or F's domain, follows; or an interaction requirement that fulfills one of these, or that sits under F itself. Anything else is reported. A step whose flow carries out no use case is left out. Add the use case to the flow's `carries_out`, or move the link to a step of the flow that carries it out.
query:
WITH carried AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT f.id AS flow, f.domain_id AS domain, c.target_id AS use_case
  FROM flow f JOIN carries_out c ON c.source_id = f.id
),
core AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT c.flow, r.id AS target FROM carried c JOIN requirement r ON r.use_case_id = c.use_case
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT c.flow, a.target_id FROM carried c JOIN applies a ON a.source_id = c.use_case
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT c.flow, pr.id FROM carried c JOIN follows fo ON fo.source_id = c.use_case JOIN pattern_rule pr ON pr.pattern_id = fo.target_id
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT c.flow, pr.id FROM carried c JOIN follows fo ON fo.source_id = c.domain JOIN pattern_rule pr ON pr.pattern_id = fo.target_id
),
inside AS (
  SELECT flow, target FROM core
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT k.flow, x.source_id FROM core k JOIN fulfills x ON x.target_id = k.target JOIN interaction_requirement ir ON ir.id = x.source_id
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT c.flow, ir.id FROM carried c JOIN interaction_requirement ir ON ir.flow_id = c.flow
)
SELECT DISTINCT s.id AS record,
       'Flow step ' || s.id || ' fulfills ' || l.target_id || ', which its flow ' || s.flow_id
       || ' does not carry out: it is not a requirement of a use case the flow carries out ('
       || (SELECT string_agg(DISTINCT c.use_case, ', ' ORDER BY c.use_case) FROM carried c WHERE c.flow = s.flow_id)
       || '), nor a domain rule one of them applies, nor a rule of a pattern one of them or the domain follows,'
       || ' nor an interaction requirement that fulfills any of these or sits under the flow.' AS message
FROM flow_step s
JOIN fulfills l ON l.source_id = s.id
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM carried c WHERE c.flow = s.flow_id)
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM inside i WHERE i.flow = s.flow_id AND i.target = l.target_id)
ORDER BY record, message

name: has-crosses-aggregate
summary: A `has_one` or `has_many` link stays inside its aggregate.
explanation: These relations link an entity to its parts, and parts belong to their aggregate, so both ends sit in the same aggregate. Only `refers_to` may cross aggregates and domains. Use `refers_to`, or move the part into the aggregate.
query:
SELECT l.source_id AS record,
       'Entity ' || l.source_id || ' ' || l.relation || ' ' || l.target_id || ', which sits in ' || t.aggregate_id
       || ', not in ' || s.aggregate_id || '; a part belongs to its aggregate, so use refers_to, or move '
       || l.target_id || ' into ' || s.aggregate_id || '.' AS message
FROM (SELECT 'has_one' AS relation, source_id, target_id FROM has_one
      UNION ALL SELECT 'has_many', source_id, target_id FROM has_many) l
JOIN entity s ON s.id = l.source_id
JOIN entity t ON t.id = l.target_id
WHERE s.aggregate_id <> t.aggregate_id
ORDER BY record, message

name: interaction-requirement-fulfills-nothing
summary: An interaction requirement names what it carries out.
explanation: An interaction requirement carries out a use case's requirement, a domain rule or a pattern rule at a view, endpoint or flow, so it links what it carries out with `fulfills`. Add the `fulfills` link.
query:
SELECT r.id AS record,
       'Interaction requirement ' || r.id || ' fulfills nothing; link the requirement or domain rule it carries out with "fulfills".' AS message
FROM interaction_requirement r
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM fulfills f WHERE f.source_id = r.id)
ORDER BY record

name: layer-order
summary: A layer's position is one that no other layer beside it has.
explanation: Layers beside each other share a parent: the domain, or the layer that holds them as sub-layers. Layers in different domains, and sub-layers of different layers, may share a position. Give each layer beside the others its own position.
query:
SELECT a.id AS record,
       'Layer ' || a.id || ' has position ' || a.position
       || CASE WHEN a.parent_layer_id IS NOT NULL THEN ' in layer ' || a.parent_layer_id ELSE ' in domain ' || a.domain_id END
       || ', the same as ' || string_agg(b.id, ', ' ORDER BY b.id)
       || CASE WHEN a.parent_layer_id IS NOT NULL THEN '; each sub-layer of a layer needs its own position.'
               ELSE '; each layer in a domain needs its own position.' END AS message
FROM layer a
JOIN layer b ON b.domain_id = a.domain_id AND b.parent_layer_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM a.parent_layer_id
            AND b.position = a.position AND b.id <> a.id
GROUP BY a.id, a.position, a.parent_layer_id, a.domain_id
ORDER BY record, message

name: lone-child
summary: A capability, a layer or a group with exactly one child, of any kind.
explanation: A level that holds one record groups nothing. Only its own children are counted, not theirs, and one with no children is not reported. A group (the `group_name` of requirements, interaction requirements, pattern rules and standard rules) is counted among its parent's children of one kind, compared trimmed and in any letter case, and reported on that parent. Merge it into a neighbor, or give it more.
query:
SELECT g.id AS record,
       upper(left(g.kind, 1)) || substr(g.kind, 2) || ' ' || g.id || ' has only one child, ' || g.child
       || '; merge it into a neighboring ' || g.kind || ', or give it more.' AS message
FROM (
  SELECT r.id, any_value(r.kind) AS kind, count(*) AS n, any_value(c.id) AS child
  FROM record_id r JOIN record_parent c ON c.parent_id = r.id
  WHERE r.kind IN ('capability', 'layer')
  GROUP BY r.id
) g
WHERE g.n = 1
UNION ALL
SELECT m.parent, upper(left(p.kind, 1)) || replace(substr(p.kind, 2), '_', ' ') || ' ' || m.parent || '''s group "' || m.label
       || '" has only one ' || replace(m.kind, '_', ' ') || ', ' || m.child || '; merge it into a neighboring group, or give it more.'
FROM (
  SELECT parent, kind, lower(trim(group_name)) AS bucket, min(trim(group_name)) AS label, count(*) AS n, any_value(id) AS child
  FROM (
    SELECT id, 'requirement' AS kind, use_case_id AS parent, group_name FROM requirement
    UNION ALL SELECT r.id, 'interaction_requirement', p.parent_id, r.group_name FROM interaction_requirement r JOIN record_parent p ON p.id = r.id
    UNION ALL SELECT id, 'pattern_rule', pattern_id, group_name FROM pattern_rule
    UNION ALL SELECT id, 'standard_rule', standard_id, group_name FROM standard_rule
  )
  WHERE group_name IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY parent, kind, lower(trim(group_name))
) m
JOIN record_id p ON p.id = m.parent
WHERE m.n = 1
ORDER BY record, message

name: manual-test-file-silent
summary: A manual test whose file exists but never mentions it.
explanation: Nothing ties the file to the test: it names neither the test's ID, nor any ID the test proves (each target of a relation whose role is `proof`), nor the test's `key` when it has one. Manual tests are not held to the automated rules (test-file-missing-id, proof-not-in-file), so a silent file is a warning: the steps a person follows should say which test they carry out. A test with a `key_file` is judged by that file instead. A missing file is test-file-missing instead. Name the test in the file, or point its `file` at the file that carries it out.
query:
SELECT f.record,
       'Manual test ' || f.record
       || CASE WHEN f.key_file IS NOT NULL THEN ' names the key file ' || f.key_file ELSE ' names the file ' || f.file END
       || ', but that file names neither ' || f.record || ' nor any ID it proves'
       || coalesce(' nor its key "' || t.key || '"', '')
       || '; name the test in the file, or point its file at the one that carries it out.' AS message
FROM file_facts f
JOIN test t ON t.id = f.record
WHERE t.state = 'manual' AND f.file_exists AND NOT coalesce(f.contains_id, false) AND f.key_file_exists IS NOT false
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM file_mentions m WHERE m.record = f.record AND m.mentioned = f.record)
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM link l
    JOIN meta_relation r ON r.name = l.relation AND r.role = 'proof'
    JOIN file_mentions m ON m.record = f.record AND m.mentioned = l.target_id
    WHERE l.source_id = f.record)
ORDER BY record

name: obligation-outside-domain
summary: An obligation that sits in no domain.
explanation: It counts in no domain's coverage, so it is reported rather than silently dropped. Lathe's own obligation kinds always sit in a domain, except a pattern rule under its pattern, which each domain that follows the pattern owes (pattern-not-followed reports a pattern nobody follows); a product's own obligation kind may not. Move the record under a domain, or declare its kind under one.
query:
SELECT o.id AS record,
       k.label || ' ' || o.id || ' sits in no domain, so no domain''s coverage counts it; move it under a domain.' AS message
FROM obligation o
JOIN record_scope s ON s.id = o.id
JOIN meta_kind k ON k.name = o.kind
WHERE s.domain_id IS NULL AND o.kind <> 'pattern_rule'
ORDER BY record

name: pattern-not-followed
summary: A pattern that no use case and no domain follows.
explanation: No domain owes its rules, so they count in no domain's coverage. Link the use cases or domains that apply it with `follows`, or remove the pattern if nothing needs it.
query:
SELECT p.id AS record,
       'No use case or domain follows pattern ' || p.id || ', so '
       || CASE p.rules WHEN 0 THEN 'it is not used anywhere.'
                       WHEN 1 THEN 'its 1 rule is not counted in any domain''s coverage.'
                       ELSE 'its ' || p.rules || ' rules are not counted in any domain''s coverage.' END AS message
FROM (SELECT p.id, (SELECT count(*) FROM pattern_rule r WHERE r.pattern_id = p.id) AS rules FROM pattern p) p
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM follows f WHERE f.target_id = p.id)
ORDER BY record

name: pattern-setting-missing
summary: A use case that follows a pattern gives each of the pattern's settings.
explanation: Each setting of the pattern (a pattern_setting row) needs a setting_value row from each use case that follows it: a value, or a reason it is not applicable. A domain that follows a pattern gives no settings. Give the missing setting a value, or say why it is not applicable.
query:
SELECT f.source_id AS record,
       'Use case ' || f.source_id || ' follows pattern ' || f.target_id || ' but gives no value for its setting "' || s.name
       || '"; give it a value, or say why it is not applicable.' AS message
FROM follows f
JOIN use_case u ON u.id = f.source_id
JOIN pattern_setting s ON s.pattern_id = f.target_id
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM setting_value v WHERE v.follower_id = f.source_id AND v.pattern_id = f.target_id AND v.setting = s.name)
ORDER BY record, message

name: proof-counts-nowhere
summary: A test whose proofs count in no domain's coverage.
explanation: A test's proof of a target counts, as in coverage, when the target is an obligation in a domain, or a pattern rule owed by the domain the test sits in (owed_pattern_rules: a domain owes a pattern rule when it follows the pattern itself, or when one of its use cases does, unless the rule is not applicable or waived there). A test is reported when it has at least one `proof` link and none of its proofs counts; the message says why for each target. The test's state does not matter: a planned test that will prove nothing counted is reported too. Point the test at an obligation that counts, or move it into the domain that owes the rule.
query:
WITH claims AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT l.source_id AS test, ts.domain_id AS test_domain, l.target_id AS target,
         tsc.domain_id AS target_domain, tp.parent_id AS target_parent,
         o.id IS NOT NULL AS obligation, o.kind = 'pattern_rule' AND tsc.domain_id IS NULL AS shared
  FROM link l
  JOIN meta_relation r ON r.name = l.relation AND r.role = 'proof'
  JOIN test t ON t.id = l.source_id
  JOIN record_scope ts ON ts.id = t.id
  JOIN record_scope tsc ON tsc.id = l.target_id
  JOIN record_parent tp ON tp.id = l.target_id
  LEFT JOIN obligation o ON o.id = l.target_id
),
judged AS (
  SELECT c.*,
    c.obligation AND CASE WHEN c.shared THEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM owed_pattern_rules o WHERE o.id = c.target AND o.domain = c.test_domain)
                          ELSE c.target_domain IS NOT NULL END AS counts,
    (SELECT string_agg(DISTINCT o.domain, ', ' ORDER BY o.domain) FROM owed_pattern_rules o WHERE o.id = c.target) AS owers
  FROM claims c
),
explained AS (
  SELECT test, counts, target || CASE
      WHEN NOT obligation THEN ' is not an obligation'
      WHEN NOT shared THEN ' sits in no domain'
      WHEN owers IS NOT NULL THEN ' is owed only by ' || owers || ', not by ' || coalesce(test_domain || ', where the test sits', 'the test, which sits in no domain')
      WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM follows f WHERE f.target_id = target_parent)
           THEN ' is owed by no domain: wherever ' || target_parent || ' is followed, its setting is not applicable or no follower meets its applies-when setting'
      ELSE ' is owed by no domain: no use case follows its pattern ' || target_parent
    END AS reason
  FROM judged
)
SELECT test AS record,
       'Test ' || test || '''s proof counts in no domain''s coverage: ' || string_agg(DISTINCT reason, '; ' ORDER BY reason)
       || '. Prove what the test''s domain owes, or move the test into a domain that owes what it proves.' AS message
FROM explained
GROUP BY test
HAVING NOT bool_or(counts)
ORDER BY record, message

name: proof-not-in-file
summary: An automated test's file names every ID the test proves, unless it names the test's own ID.
explanation: Each target of a relation whose role is `proof` must appear in the file, as a whole ID, when the file does not name the test's own ID. Each proved ID the file leaves out is one error. A test whose file names its own ID vouches for all its claims; a test with a `key` is checked by test-file-missing-id instead. A test with a `key_file` is judged by that file; a key file that is missing or outside the root is test-file-missing only. A `supports` link is not a proof claim, so its target need not appear. Manual and planned tests are not checked here. Name the ID in the test's name in the file, name the test's own ID there, or remove the claim.
query:
SELECT DISTINCT f.record,
       'Test ' || f.record || ' proves ' || l.target_id || ', but its '
       || CASE WHEN f.key_file IS NOT NULL THEN 'key file ' || f.key_file ELSE 'file ' || f.file END
       || ' names neither ' || f.record || ' nor ' || l.target_id
       || '; name the test''s ID, or every ID it proves, in that file.' AS message
FROM file_facts f
JOIN test t ON t.id = f.record
JOIN link l ON l.source_id = f.record
JOIN meta_relation r ON r.name = l.relation AND r.role = 'proof'
WHERE f.file_exists AND NOT f.contains_id AND f.key_file_exists IS NOT false AND t.state = 'automated' AND t.key IS NULL
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM file_mentions m WHERE m.record = f.record AND m.mentioned = l.target_id)
ORDER BY record, message

name: proof-still-owed
summary: An obligation that is already proved, but that a planned test is also meant to prove.
explanation: Coverage counts these in `planned_any` but not in `planned`; this check names each one, with the planned test that still owes its proof, so the list behind `planned_any` is never only a count. An obligation not yet proved whose test is only planned is reported by unproved instead. Proof is judged as coverage judges it (coverage_item): a pattern rule is owed per domain, and only tests in that domain prove it there or owe it there. Write the planned test, or drop its claim if the proof it owes is already made.
query:
SELECT DISTINCT i.id AS record,
       upper(left(i.kind, 1)) || replace(substr(i.kind, 2), '_', ' ') || ' ' || i.id || ' is proved'
       || CASE WHEN i.per_domain THEN ' in ' || i.domain ELSE '' END
       || ', but planned test ' || p.source || CASE WHEN i.per_domain THEN ' there' ELSE '' END
       || ' still owes a proof of it; write that test, or drop its proves link to ' || i.id || '.' AS message
FROM coverage_item i
JOIN role_link p ON p.target = i.id AND p.role = 'proof' AND p.state = 'planned'
                AND (NOT i.per_domain OR p.source_domain = i.domain)
WHERE i.proved
ORDER BY record, message

name: raised-by-outside-aggregate
summary: A domain event's `raised_by` names an entity of the event's own aggregate.
explanation: An event is raised by its aggregate, so the entity whose change raises it is one of that aggregate's entities. What another aggregate does about the event is said by its `reacts_to`. Point `raised_by` at an entity of the event's aggregate, or move the event under the aggregate that raises it.
query:
SELECT r.source_id AS record,
       'Event ' || r.source_id || ' is raised_by ' || r.target_id || ', which sits in ' || n.aggregate_id
       || ', not in the event''s aggregate ' || e.aggregate_id || '; point raised_by at an entity of ' || e.aggregate_id
       || ', or move the event under the aggregate that raises it.' AS message
FROM raised_by r
JOIN domain_event e ON e.id = r.source_id
JOIN entity n ON n.id = r.target_id
WHERE n.aggregate_id <> e.aggregate_id
ORDER BY record, message

name: rule-not-applied
summary: A domain rule that no use case applies.
explanation: A rule that nothing applies is either missing from a use case's `applies` links or no longer needed. Link the use cases that rely on it with `applies`, or remove the rule.
query:
SELECT r.id AS record,
       'Domain rule ' || r.id || ' is not applied by any use case; link it with "applies" from each use case that relies on it, or remove it.' AS message
FROM domain_rule r
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM applies a WHERE a.target_id = r.id)
ORDER BY record

name: section-stage-mismatch
summary: A kind's folder belongs to the kind's own stage.
explanation: A Define kind sits in a Define folder and a Design kind in a Design folder. A product-level folder, with no stage (such as shared), may hold a kind of any stage. Lathe's own kinds always fit; a product's own kind may not. Change the product kind's `section` or `stage`.
query:
SELECT NULL AS record,
       'Kind "' || k.name || '" is in stage "' || coalesce(k.stage::VARCHAR, '') || '", but its folder "' || k.section
       || '" belongs to stage "' || s.stage || '".' AS message
FROM meta_kind k
JOIN meta_section s ON s.name = k.section
WHERE s.stage IS NOT NULL AND k.stage IS DISTINCT FROM s.stage
ORDER BY message

name: standard-rule-unmet
summary: A standard rule that nothing meets.
explanation: A standard rule asks nothing of a domain, so it owes no coverage, but a rule that no component, technical step or test `meets` has no use the spec can see, and nothing outlives its purpose. Link what follows the rule to it with `meets`, or remove the rule.
query:
SELECT r.id AS record,
       'Nothing meets standard rule ' || r.id || ' (' || r.title || '). Link a component, technical step or test that '
       || 'follows it with meets, or remove it.' AS message
FROM standard_rule r
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM meets m WHERE m.target_id = r.id)
ORDER BY record

name: step-order
summary: The steps on each path of a flow are numbered 1, 2, 3 and so on, without gaps.
explanation: The steps of a flow (flow_step) and of a technical flow (design_step) are read in `position` within their `path`, a short name such as main or refused, compared trimmed and in any letter case. The schema gives each step a whole number that no other step on its path has; a path whose positions skip a number is reported once, on the first step after the gap. Renumber the steps of the path to close the gap.
query:
WITH steps AS (
  SELECT s.id, s.flow_id AS parent, lower(trim(s.path)) AS step_path, s.position AS n, k.label, lower(fk.label) AS flow_label
  FROM flow_step s, meta_kind k, meta_kind fk WHERE k.name = 'flow_step' AND fk.name = 'flow'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT s.id, s.design_flow_id, lower(trim(s.path)), s.position, k.label, lower(fk.label)
  FROM design_step s, meta_kind k, meta_kind fk WHERE k.name = 'design_step' AND fk.name = 'design_flow'
),
paths AS (
  SELECT parent, step_path, max(n) AS top FROM steps GROUP BY parent, step_path
),
gaps AS (
  SELECT p.parent, p.step_path, min(m) AS first_missing, string_agg(m::VARCHAR, ', ' ORDER BY m) AS missing_list
  FROM paths p CROSS JOIN range(1, p.top) t(m)
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM steps x WHERE x.parent = p.parent AND x.step_path = p.step_path AND x.n = t.m)
  GROUP BY p.parent, p.step_path
)
SELECT s.id AS record,
       s.label || ' ' || s.id || ' has position ' || s.n
       || CASE WHEN s.step_path = 'main' THEN '' ELSE ' on path ' || s.step_path END
       || ' in ' || s.flow_label || ' ' || s.parent || ', but no step'
       || CASE WHEN s.step_path = 'main' THEN '' ELSE ' of that path' END || ' has position ' || g.missing_list
       || '; number the steps of ' || CASE WHEN s.step_path = 'main' THEN 'a ' || s.flow_label ELSE 'a path' END
       || ' 1, 2, 3 and so on, with no gaps.' AS message
FROM gaps g
JOIN steps s ON s.parent = g.parent AND s.step_path = g.step_path
WHERE s.n = (SELECT min(x.n) FROM steps x WHERE x.parent = g.parent AND x.step_path = g.step_path AND x.n > g.first_missing)
ORDER BY record, message

name: test-file-missing
summary: A test's `file`, and its `key_file` when it names one, exists.
explanation: For an automated or manual test a missing file is an error. A planned test may name the file it will live in, so for it a missing file is a warning, as for a component whose file does not exist yet. A `key_file` (the file that holds the test's key, when the test runs from a shared class in another file) must be a file under the product root; one outside it is always an error. Fix the path (relative to the repo root), or write the file.
query:
SELECT CASE WHEN t.state = 'planned' THEN 'warning' ELSE 'error' END AS severity, f.record,
       'Test ' || f.record || ' names the file ' || f.file || ', which does not exist'
       || CASE WHEN t.state = 'planned' THEN ' yet.' ELSE '.' END AS message
FROM file_facts f JOIN test t ON t.id = f.record
WHERE NOT f.file_exists
UNION ALL
SELECT CASE WHEN t.state = 'planned' AND f.key_file_inside THEN 'warning' ELSE 'error' END, f.record,
       'Test ' || f.record || ' names the key file ' || f.key_file || ', which '
       || CASE WHEN NOT f.key_file_inside THEN 'is outside the product root; name a file under it.'
               WHEN t.state = 'planned' THEN 'does not exist yet.'
               ELSE 'does not exist.' END
FROM file_facts f JOIN test t ON t.id = f.record
WHERE f.key_file IS NOT NULL AND NOT f.key_file_exists
ORDER BY record, message

name: test-file-missing-id
summary: An automated test's file names the test, so the code can be traced back to it.
explanation:
The file must name the test's own ID, or else every ID the test proves (each target of a relation whose role is `proof`); a missing proved ID is proof-not-in-file. This check reports the two cases that leave no proved ID to name: a test with a `key` whose file does not contain that key text (the ID rules then do not apply), and a test that proves no record and whose file does not name its own ID.

A test that proves no record but `supports` one (a check of a mechanism that backs an obligation without proving it) is not reported: support is never proof, so its file owes no ID. A test with a `key_file` is judged by that file instead of `file`; a key file that is missing or outside the root is test-file-missing only. Manual and planned tests are not checked here. Put the test's ID in the test's name in the file, or fix its `key` or `key_file`.
query:
SELECT f.record,
       'Test ' || f.record
       || CASE WHEN f.key_file IS NOT NULL THEN ' names the key file ' || f.key_file ELSE ' names the file ' || f.file END
       || ', but that file '
       || CASE WHEN t.key IS NOT NULL THEN 'does not contain its key "' || t.key || '".'
               ELSE 'does not mention ' || f.record || ', and the test proves no record whose ID it could name instead.' END AS message
FROM file_facts f JOIN test t ON t.id = f.record
WHERE f.file_exists AND NOT f.contains_id AND f.key_file_exists IS NOT false AND t.state = 'automated'
  AND (t.key IS NOT NULL OR (
    NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM link l JOIN meta_relation r ON r.name = l.relation AND r.role = 'proof' WHERE l.source_id = t.id)
    AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM supports s WHERE s.source_id = t.id)))
ORDER BY record

name: test-proves-nothing
summary: A test that proves, and supports, nothing.
explanation: A test exists to prove obligations (a link of a `proof` relation such as `proves`) or to check a mechanism that backs one (`supports`). One with neither has no purpose the spec can see: running a flow (`runs`) or exercising a component (`covers`) says what it touches, not what it shows. Link the obligation it proves with "proves", or the one it backs with "supports", or remove the test.
query:
SELECT t.id AS record,
       'Test ' || t.id || ' proves nothing and supports nothing; link the obligation it proves with "proves", '
       || 'or the one it backs with "supports", or remove it.' AS message
FROM test t
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM link l JOIN meta_relation r ON r.name = l.relation
                  WHERE l.source_id = t.id AND (r.role = 'proof' OR r.name = 'supports'))
ORDER BY record

name: test-type-mismatch
summary: A test's `test_type` does not suit what it proves.
explanation: Kept conservative: only a test of type domain_rule that proves requirements and no domain rule, or a test of type acceptance that proves domain rules and no requirement, is reported. A unit test may prove either, so it is not reported, nor is any other type, nor a test that proves both. Change the type, or what the test proves.
query:
SELECT t.id AS record,
       'Test ' || t.id || ' has test_type ' || t.test_type || ' but proves only '
       || CASE WHEN t.test_type = 'acceptance' THEN 'domain rules' ELSE 'use case requirements' END
       || ' (' || t.targets || '); '
       || CASE WHEN t.test_type = 'acceptance'
               THEN 'an acceptance test proves requirements, so give it test_type domain_rule, or correct what it proves.'
               ELSE 'a domain_rule test proves domain rules, so give it test_type acceptance, or correct what it proves.' END AS message
FROM (
  SELECT t.id, t.test_type, string_agg(DISTINCT p.target_id, ', ' ORDER BY p.target_id) AS targets,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE o.kind = 'requirement') AS requirements,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE o.kind = 'domain_rule') AS rules
  FROM test t
  JOIN proves p ON p.source_id = t.id
  JOIN obligation o ON o.id = p.target_id
  GROUP BY t.id, t.test_type
) t
WHERE (t.test_type = 'domain_rule' AND t.requirements > 0 AND t.rules = 0)
   OR (t.test_type = 'acceptance' AND t.rules > 0 AND t.requirements = 0)
ORDER BY record

name: too-many-children
summary: A record with more children of one kind than its product's max_children setting.
explanation: The setting is the product's product_setting row (15 when it has none). A parent with that many children of one kind is missing a level between them, such as a capability, a layer or another aggregate. Children are counted per kind. Tests are exempt: the app groups them by what they prove, so they are never shown as one list. The steps of a flow or a technical flow are counted per path, since each path reads as its own list, and requirements, interaction requirements, pattern rules and standard rules per `group_name`, since each group reads under its own heading; the ungrouped ones are one list. Paths and groups are compared trimmed and in any letter case. Add a level, or a group, and move the children into it.
query:
WITH children AS (
  SELECT p.id, p.kind, p.parent_id,
         coalesce(fs.path, ds.path, rq.group_name, ir.group_name, pr.group_name, sr.group_name, '') AS label
  FROM record_parent p
  LEFT JOIN flow_step fs ON fs.id = p.id
  LEFT JOIN design_step ds ON ds.id = p.id
  LEFT JOIN requirement rq ON rq.id = p.id
  LEFT JOIN interaction_requirement ir ON ir.id = p.id
  LEFT JOIN pattern_rule pr ON pr.id = p.id
  LEFT JOIN standard_rule sr ON sr.id = p.id
  WHERE p.parent_id IS NOT NULL AND p.kind <> 'test'
),
counted AS (
  SELECT parent_id, kind, lower(trim(label)) AS bucket, min(trim(label)) AS label, count(*) AS n
  FROM children GROUP BY parent_id, kind, lower(trim(label))
)
SELECT c.parent_id AS record,
       upper(left(p.kind, 1)) || replace(substr(p.kind, 2), '_', ' ') || ' ' || c.parent_id || ' has ' || c.n
       || ' children of kind ' || c.kind
       || CASE WHEN c.kind IN ('flow_step', 'design_step') AND c.bucket <> 'main' THEN ' on path ' || c.label
               WHEN c.kind NOT IN ('flow_step', 'design_step') AND c.bucket <> '' THEN ' in group ' || c.label ELSE '' END
       || ', more than the ' || coalesce(ps.max_children, 15)
       || ' that the product''s max_children setting allows; add a level between them, such as a capability, a layer or another aggregate.' AS message
FROM counted c
JOIN record_id p ON p.id = c.parent_id
JOIN record_scope s ON s.id = c.parent_id
LEFT JOIN product_setting ps ON ps.product_id = s.product_id
WHERE c.n > coalesce(ps.max_children, 15)
ORDER BY record, message

name: unproved
summary: An obligation that no automated or manual test proves yet.
explanation: A test proves an obligation through a `proof` link such as `proves`; a planned test is not proof. A pattern rule is owed by the domains owed_pattern_rules names (each domain that follows its pattern, unless the rule is not applicable or waived there), and only a test in that domain proves it there, so it is reported once for each domain that owes it and lacks one. An automated test's proof counts only when its file backs it, as in coverage: the file names the test's own ID (or its key), or names that target; an unbacked claim is also a proof-not-in-file error. Write a test that `proves` it, and name the test in its file.
query:
SELECT DISTINCT i.id AS record,
       CASE WHEN i.per_domain
            THEN 'Pattern rule ' || i.id || ' is not proved in ' || i.domain
                 || CASE WHEN i.planned_proof THEN ' yet: its test there is only planned.'
                         ELSE ': no test in ' || i.domain || ' proves it, though the domain follows its pattern.' END
            ELSE 'No test proves ' || replace(i.kind, '_', ' ') || ' ' || i.id
                 || CASE WHEN i.planned_proof THEN ' yet: its test is only planned.' ELSE '.' END END AS message
FROM coverage_item i
WHERE NOT i.proved
ORDER BY record, message

name: unsatisfied
summary: An obligation that no design link targets yet.
explanation: An obligation is any record of a kind the schema marks as one (the obligation supertype). A proof-only obligation kind, such as a pattern rule, asks for no design, so it is never reported. An obligation of a full kind is owed by its domain and designed by a link of a `design` relation such as `satisfies`, as coverage counts it (coverage_item). Link a component to it with `satisfies`, or another design relation.
query:
SELECT DISTINCT i.id AS record,
       CASE WHEN i.per_domain
            THEN 'Pattern rule ' || i.id || ' is not designed in ' || i.domain || ': no component in ' || i.domain
                 || ' satisfies it, though the domain follows its pattern.'
            ELSE 'Nothing designs ' || replace(i.kind, '_', ' ') || ' ' || i.id || ': no component satisfies it.' END AS message
FROM coverage_item i
WHERE NOT i.designed
ORDER BY record, message

name: use-case-outside-capability
summary: Once a domain has capabilities, each of its use cases sits in one of them.
explanation: A use case left directly under the domain is missing from the domain's use case index. Move it under one of the domain's capabilities; its ID does not change. A domain with no capabilities is not reported.
query:
SELECT u.id AS record,
       'Use case ' || u.id || ' sits directly under domain ' || u.domain_id
       || ', which has capabilities; move it under the capability it belongs to.' AS message
FROM use_case u
WHERE u.capability_id IS NULL
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM capability c WHERE c.domain_id = u.domain_id)
ORDER BY record

name: use-case-without-flow
summary: Once a domain has flows, each of its use cases is carried out by one.
explanation: A flow names the use cases it carries out with `carries_out`. A domain with no flows is not reported: its interaction design has not started. Link the flow that carries the use case out, or write a flow for it.
query:
SELECT u.id AS record,
       'Use case ' || u.id || ' is not carried out by any flow, though domain ' || u.domain_id
       || ' has flows; link the flow that carries it out with "carries_out".' AS message
FROM use_case u
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM flow f WHERE f.domain_id = u.domain_id)
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM carries_out c WHERE c.target_id = u.id)
ORDER BY record

name: use-case-without-requirements
summary: A use case with no requirements under it yet.
explanation: A use case's requirements are the rules it must follow, so one with none says nothing checkable. A use case that follows a pattern is left out: its rules come from the pattern's rules, so it may have no requirements of its own. Add requirements under it, or have it follow the pattern it applies.
query:
SELECT u.id AS record, 'Use case ' || u.id || ' has no requirements.' AS message
FROM use_case u
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM requirement r WHERE r.use_case_id = u.id)
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM follows f WHERE f.source_id = u.id)
ORDER BY record
